title: Best YouTube Intro and Outro Makers (2026): How to Hire One
h1: Best Intro and Outro Video Creators
description: How to hire someone to make YouTube intros and outros: what the package should include, length, end screens, price factors and red flags.
intro: An intro opens your videos with your channel's look, and an outro, or end screen, invites viewers to watch more or subscribe. Good ones are short, on-brand and designed around the platform's layout. They go wrong when they are too long, use unlicensed music, or leave no space for YouTube's end screen elements. This guide helps you order intros and outros that viewers will not skip.

faq.q: How long should an intro be?
faq.a: Short. Many viewers leave in the first seconds, so a brief branded moment after a strong opening hook usually works better than a long animation at the very start.
It is the last part of a YouTube video where you can place clickable elements such as other videos and a subscribe button. An outro should leave space for them in the positions YouTube allows.
Often. Make sure it is licensed for use on monetized YouTube videos, or use music from a library you already license.

faq.q: Can I get a template to reuse?
faq.a: Ask for a version where you can change the title or text, or for a source file if you edit your own videos.

faq.q: Should intros match my thumbnails and channel art?
faq.a: Yes. Consistent colors, fonts and logo across intros, thumbnails and channel art help viewers recognize your content.
